messages:
ravi: Quick follow-up from the hybrid priority multiplexing RFC I posted this morning — TL;DR: we need a concrete plan for mixing short low-token requests with long streaming/LLM|stream sessions without starving either class. Thoughts?
elaine: Important callout: we saw short requests experience p99 latency spikes when a single long stream hogged a slot in last week's test.
ravi: Yep. Repro: run synthetic with 1:10 long:short, long sessions hold KV cache and GPU slot for ~30s. Short requests (<=50 tokens) jump from 30ms to 600ms p99.
chris: Agree we should avoid strict FIFO. Two quick interface options: 1) weighted multiplex where short requests have weight 10x; 2) preemptible slices where long sessions voluntarily yield mini-slices every N tokens.
ravi: Option 1 is simplest to implement in the router. Weighting means dynamic queue where admission decisions use effective weight*age scoring. But fairness math gets messy at scale.
elaine: Option 2 requires runtime support for cooperative yielding and fast context save/restore. Complexity on backend but gives predictable latency for short jobs.
chris: Also consider hybrid: soft-slice long sessions at kernel level (e.g., max continuous decode 4k tokens or 2s) + admission weighting to prioritize short requests. That reduces context thrashing while giving guarantees.
infra-bot: perf-test reminder: run perf-suite/priority-mux with flags --slice-ms=2000 --short-weight=8 to reproduce baseline.
ravi: Tradeoffs we discussed: latency SLOs for short requests vs throughput efficiency for long sessions. More slices -> higher throughput loss due to KV cache churn.
elaine: Measured on rtx-cluster-3 last week: 250ms slices doubled token throughput loss ~8-10% compared to no-slicing; but p99 short latency dropped from 600ms to 120ms.
chris: If we expose configuration per-customer (Dedicated tier) we can let high-throughput customers choose throughput-optimized (no-slice) mode and PLG customers use latency-optimized slices.
ravi: Good product angle. Need safety/backstop: global admission should still protect critical system lanes (health-checks, controlplane).
elaine: Implementation plan suggestion: phase 1 router-side weighted admission + soft admission caps per model variant (fast to ship). Phase 2 add voluntary runtime yields (slice checkpoints) for models supporting it.
chris: API surface: add 'priority_hint' in request metadata (SHORT | NORMAL | LONG) and server-side default heuristic based on token budget. Keep backward-compatible default to NORMAL.
ravi: For metrics/observability we should surface: per-priority p50/p95/p99 latency, slice_count, preemptions, cache_warm_hit_pct. Will help tune weight values.
elaine: I'll prototype router admission logic this week. Chris, can you spec the runtime checkpoint trampoline? Need API for 'yield_point' that runtime can call and router can reschedule.
chris: On it. I'll paste a sketch later today.
infra-bot: action: create perf job 'hybrid-mux-experiment-v1' scheduled nightly. Owner: elaine.
ravi: Decision for now: pursue hybrid approach staged rollout. Phase1 (weighting + per-customer policy) target in 2 sprints. Phase2 (runtime yields) exploratory spike concurrently.
elaine: Ack. Will open PR for admission changes and a tracking RFC for runtime yields.
chris: Minor note: quantify cache-warm penalty per-slice for 1B vs 7B models — might influence defaults.
ravi: Good point. Elaine, add model-size param to perf job.
elaine: Will do.
ravi: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD I'll post follow-up RFC with action items and timelines. :thumbsup:
